messages:
maria: FYI - Acme is seeing recurring auth 429s and bill spikes on their Dedicated pool eu-west-2 this morning. p95 token latency up ~4x.
sam_acme: yep, started around 07:12 UTC. we got a bunch of 429s during a steady inference traffic window, and our invoice shows a big jump for token count at the same time.
maria: Can you paste an example error and the pool id? Also did you change model/parallelism?
sam_acme: pool id: rdw-ded-eu2-77, model: redwood-13b-q4, no config change on our side. example curl response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and body: `{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 12 }`.
jordan_oncall: assigning. @alex_runtime can you check for noisy-slice / MIG neighbor activity on that host group? possible autoscaler thrash?
alex_runtime: Looking. Early read shows one node with 3 small MIG slices hitting SM/util ~98% and a different tenant spiking concurrent streams. Could be thermal or SM saturation causing request queuing which looks like auth 429s from client side due to request timeouts/retries.
emily_infra: I pulled fabric and perf counters. There's consistent peer bandwidth spikes on node n-eu2-14 between 07:10-07:25. NVLink counters show transient congestion. No OOM logs.
ops-bot: deploy alert: autoscaler bumped rdw-ded-eu2-77 by +2 slices at 07:15 UTC due to p95 targets.
maria: So autoscaler increased capacity but billing also jumped. Could be double counting retries + cache warmups. Sam — did your client retry aggressively on 429s?
sam_acme: yes we have an exponential backoff but were re-sending a few times within 15s window until success. Not huge but enough.
alex_runtime: Hypothesis: noisy neighbor caused tail latency -> client retries -> autoscaler sees high latency and ramps -> additional compute + warmup token emission -> higher billed tokens. Need to confirm whether retries were counted as extra tokens (they are) and whether KV cache misses during scale-up increased token generation.
jordan_oncall: Action items: 1) replicate load on a staging node with same MIG packing, 2) checkout MIG partitioning on rdw-ded-eu2-77 for colocated tenants, 3) temporarily isolate Acme to a new slice to confirm mitigation.
emily_infra: I'll run an isolation move to a clean slice. scheduling a live migration at 07:50 UTC — slight disruption expected.
sam_acme: appreciated. please keep it short, we're watching revenue-sensitive workloads.
maria: While emily moves them, can alex provide short repro steps for runtime team and a quick check-list we can run on affected nodes?
alex_runtime: Repro steps (quick):
```
# simulate multi-tenant noise
wrk -c 60 -t 8 -d 5m --script=tail-burst.lua http://<ded-slice-ip>/v1/generate
# run customer's steady traffic in parallel
wrk -c 12 -t 2 -d 5m http://<ded-slice-ip>/v1/generate
# collect metrics: nvlink, sm_util, p99 latency
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1
curl -s http://<metrics>/node/n-eu2-14 | jq '.gpu_counters'
```
Expected: high SM util on neighbor, increased p99 latency on customer's requests, token count jump due to retries/warmup.

alex_runtime: Quick checks for support:
- confirm `retry_after` pattern in logs, count retries per request-id
- token_count deltas pre/post 07:10
- autoscaler events/log: scale decision timestamps
- MIG split on node: `nvidia-smi mig -L` to map slices

emily_infra: Isolation started. moving Acme off n-eu2-14 -> n-eu2-21 at 07:50.
ops-bot: migration job 87431: started (rdw-ded-eu2-77 -> rdw-ded-eu2-77-slice-21)
emily_infra: Migration completed at 07:52. Initial health checks OK.
sam_acme: initial traffic looks stable, auth 429s gone within ~2 minutes of migration. p95 back to baseline.
maria: Nice. Can we mark this as noisy-neighbor-cause and follow up with a mitigation plan to prevent billing thrash?
alex_runtime: Recommend: 1) more aggressive isolation thresholds for autoscaler (don't scale on short tail spikes), 2) adopt per-tenant retry budgeting to avoid multiplier billing, 3) improved KV cache prewarming for scale-up to reduce warmup tokens.
jordan_oncall: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-314 with timeline and mitigation suggestions. Assign to eng-runtime and infra for follow-up.
maria: Sam, sorry about the disruption. We'll include a billing review and credit any obvious retry-driven overages. I'll loop in finance after the postmortem.
sam_acme: thanks all. please paste the incident ticket when ready.
maria: will do. thanks everyone :heart:
